findings.expected_vs_actual: Expected the D-5 rule (largestPot includes the returned uncalled chips) to be pinned by a repository test. Actually, reverting largestPot to awards only leaves every test in tests/engine, tests/table, tests/playtest and tests/ui green, because no seed in the suites has its largest pot end with a return. The behaviour itself is correct: the judge observed largestPot $6 for a walk and $36 for a flop fold-to-raise.
findings.fix: Optional: add a summarize unit case on a walk whose largestPot must be 6.

findings.expected_vs_actual: Code-review gap: no repository test plays an exact-stack all-in call to the end of the hand. The judge's own check shows the behaviour holds. In S-A with seat 3 at $8, the exact flop call is followed by seat 1 calling and the hand checked down; at showdown returned is absent, the award is $24 (the sum of totalContribution) and checkState is []. With seat 1 folded preflop, the exact call runs out the board at once, with nothing returned and an award of $16.
findings.fix: Optional: extend the exactCall unit case to the end of the hand and assert returned is undefined and the award equals the sum of totalContribution.

summary: Every engine, checker and UI-text item passes. The new behaviour checks out end to end with the judge's own scenarios. A 6000-hand random fuzz with short stacks (3–7 seats, 4-bet cap respected) found 0 checkStep violations, chips conserved, returned equal to top minus second total contribution, toAct never all-in or folded, allIn exactly when an unfolded seat has stack 0, and every showdown with a 5-card board. Of 12 source mutants, the repository suite kills 11; the survivor is the D-5 playtest largestPot line (LOW, J-1-01). The 10k playtest output is byte-identical to base. The e2e specs pass in both browsers. CI is green. The only open item is SPEC-16's story doc, which the Documentor has not published yet. No blocking findings.
